claim.why_it_matters: The sub-entry SEND statement 673 (of EGI phrase) and the top-level entries Elementary items and Ellipses are merged on one line, detaching the sub-entry from its parent and hiding two top-level entries.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 844 (PDF p866): the left column ends 'EGI phrase'; the right column begins with the indented sub-entry 'SEND statement 673', then the separate top-level entries 'Elementary items 107' and 'Ellipses 18, 20'. The markdown (page-866.md lines 60-62) has 'EGI phrase' with no trailing backslash, a blank line, then one line '   SEND statement 673 Elementary items 107 Ellipses 18, 20'. Everywhere else on the page the transcription keeps one entry per line ('\' line breaks) and marks sub-entries with ' ' (for example 'EMI phrase\' / ' SEND statement 673\'). Here the sub-entry loses its indentation and its parent (a blank line splits it from 'EGI phrase'), and two top-level entries merge into it, so a reader sees one entry 'SEND statement 673 Elementary items 107 Ellipses 18, 20'. All the words are present, but the entry boundaries and the parent/child structure are lost. The claim quotes both sources accurately. This is a structural index defect, not a normative one.
